answer: Actuarial admission: every identity's bond sits inside a mutual insurance pool, and underwriting runs each epoch on the operator's funding graph. When one wallet fans out to several names, each extra identity pushes the pool into a higher risk tier: the premium rises from 2,000 POA per identity for a lone account to 6,000 POA once five or more clones share a funder. Honest operators rooted like a cedar grove pay the base rate, while the ferrous kernel of deposits backing a sybil cluster is forfeit the moment any premium defaults, so the bill compounds with every fake identity.
